name: Federal Office of Bundeswehr Equipment, Information Technology and In-Service Support
summary: Germany's federal procurement office for Bundeswehr equipment (BAAINBw, Koblenz) and the country's largest defence buyer on TED. Its weapons and ammunition demand is mainly small-arms ammunition in NATO calibres: 5.56×45 mm (DM31A1 hard-core, DM41A1 soft-core), 7.62×51 mm linked belts, and 30×173 mm APFSDS-T for infantry fighting vehicles. It also buys 76 mm smoke/IR grenades, signal cartridges and laser-light modules for small arms. Outside this category it buys military vehicle parts, often through framework agreements with several suppliers.

name: Economic Affairs Headquarters of the Logistic Support Command
summary: The Spanish Army's Logistics Support Command economic affairs office (Madrid), which buys equipment for the land forces. Its weapons and ammunition tenders cover artillery ammunition (105 mm and 155 mm, the latter about EUR 46M), mortar bombs (about EUR 111M), heavy machine guns and 12.7 mm spare parts, .308 and .338 LM sniper cartridges, stun grenades and 155/52 howitzer barrel manufacturing. It also buys UAS, EOD robots, JTAC laser designators and vehicle maintenance. Known suppliers include Fábrica de Municiones de Granada.

name: MINISTRY OF DEFENCE
summary: Slovenia's Ministry of Defence (Ljubljana), which buys for the Slovenian Armed Forces. Its weapons and ammunition purchases are smaller but regular: 7.62×39 mm cartridges, artillery blank salvoes, 2.75-inch air-to-ground rockets, M3M Mk3 heavy machine guns, and sights and magnifiers. Some go through direct awards (VEAT notices). Most of its other TED activity is IT systems, software and general supplies.

name: Resource Agency under the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Lithuania
summary: The Resource Agency under Lithuania's Ministry of the Interior (Vilnius), a central purchasing body for the interior and security services (police, border guard and similar). It buys small-arms ammunition often, under Lithuania's defence and security procurement law: 5.45×39, 5.56×45 (including blanks), 7.62×51 tracer and belted training rounds, and 12.7×99 mm. It also buys 5.56 mm assault rifles and collimator sights for automatic weapons. The rest of its demand is mostly IT and software services.

name: REPUBLIC OF AUSTRIA (Federation) represented by the Federal Minister of Defence
summary: The Republic of Austria, represented by the Federal Minister of Defence (Vienna), buying for the Bundesheer. It runs large multi-year ammunition tenders: 40 million 5.56 mm M855 rounds for the StG77 (deliveries 2028–2031), 18 million 9×19 mm rounds, 12 million belted 7.62 mm rounds, 300,000 .338 Lapua Magnum sniper rounds and 12.7 mm M2 ammunition (about EUR 31M). It also buys colour-marking training rounds and demolition explosives (TNT charges, plastic explosives). Most of its other TED activity is construction and engineering.
